opening_message:
Ticket 1: Belinda Fuentes (employee ID E039) requests admin access to Payroll.

Team memory: 2 note(s) about employee E039.
Note 1 (ticket 1), written by HR agent:
  - role: Analyst
  - employment type: full_time
  - recommendation for Payroll: write
  - comment: Belinda Fuentes (E039) is a full-time Analyst. Requested admin to Payroll; as a full-time employee, admin is only granted if the employee's role owns the system (Payroll Specialist), so the maximum is write. Recommend write.
Note 2 (ticket 1), written by Security agent:
  - role: Analyst
  - employment type: contractor
  - security training: basic
  - recommendation for Payroll: read
  - comment: Security DB check: E039 is a contractor with basic security training. Max access for a contractor with basic training is read; admin is never allowed. Requested admin, so recommend read. Note: this conflicts with the HR note listing full-time; going with Security DB record.
reason: Belinda Fuentes (E039) requested admin access to Payroll. The Security DB record (treated as authoritative per the Security agent's note) identifies her as a contractor with basic security training. Per policy, contractors may have at most read, or write only with advanced training, and never admin. Since her requested level (admin) is above her maximum (read), I grant the maximum allowed: read.

content.text:
Let me analyze this ticket.

Employee E039 (Belinda Fuentes) requests admin access to Payroll.

There are two notes with conflicting information:
- HR note: role Analyst, employment type full_time. Recommendation: write. HR says full-time employees max is write (admin only if role owns system; Analyst doesn't own Payroll, Payroll Specialist does).
- Security note: role Analyst, employment type contractor, security training basic. Recommendation: read. Security says contractor with basic training max is read; admin never allowed. Security DB record says contractor.

The Security agent notes the conflict and says they're going with the Security DB record.

As the Approver, I need to make a decision. The notes say Security agent wrote that they're going with Security DB record. Which is authoritative? The team memory implies the Security agent's DB is the authoritative source. Hmm.

Both notes agree on requested: admin. HR recommends write (if full-time), Security recommends read (if contractor with basic training).

If full-time Analyst: max is write (admin only if role owns system; Analyst doesn't own Payroll). Requested admin > max write, so grant write.
If contractor with basic training: max is read (contractor read, or write if advanced training; never admin). Requested admin > max read, so grant read.

The conflict: which employment type to trust? The Security agent explicitly noted the conflict and said "going with Security DB record" meaning contractor with basic training.

I should decide based on the information. The decision should be read, as the Security DB record is treated as authoritative, and the security agent recommends read.

Actually, let me think carefully. The policy: contractor employees: read, or write if they have advanced security training. Never admin. Belinda has basic training, so max = read. Requested admin, so grant read.

So the decision is read.

I'll submit decision with level "read" and reason citing that Security DB indicates contractor with basic training, max read, admin not allowed, requested admin so grant maximum read.
